problem.title: Hypothesis (S): are a composite's twistor slots fermionic modes
problem.source: T12, successor problem (6); maintainer decisions of 23 and 26 October and Leon's decision of 31 October
problem.statement: Hypothesis (S) is derived (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) from the slot-module hypothesis (\claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}): a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, hypercharge from the centre, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system. Derive the remaining clauses from stated structure (the single doublet of slot creation operators, the joint Clifford system, and the chirality clause, whose content beyond the other clauses and anomaly freedom is the choice of the empty state as the particle half's neutral singlet, now placed on the chain's Pati-Salam stage), or record which of them remain premises.
problem.why: The lepton doublet, the common handedness of doublets and singlets, $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, the values $3/8$ and $3/4$, and every result naming a species rest on it; without it the tensor state space contains no lepton, and the families and neutrino papers must re-examine what they import.
problem.known:
CPT closure of a slot module tensored with the pair system, with hypercharge from the centre, holds exactly for $F \cong a\Lambda^{0}\C^{2} \oplus b\Lambda^{1}\C^{2} \oplus a\Lambda^{2}\C^{2}$; with one vacuum, anomaly-free halvings need $b$ odd, the extra doublets entering in vectorlike pairs; for a slot module generated from its vacuum by one doublet, CPT closure alone forces the fermionic module with exclusion; and for that module anomaly freedom forces the chirality $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ except for a free line in the neutral-singlet block (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}). On that basis the premise was restated (23 October). The clause fixing the neutral-singlet line, first stated as commuting with $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, is now stated as "the chirality is the grading of the joint Clifford system" (every slot and pair Majorana generator is odd for it), proved equivalent for a CPT halving; version 3 of the premise (26 October). Its content beyond the other clauses is known exactly (\claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}). On the five-mode module the gauge algebra, the number-conserving bilinears $\mathfrak{u}(5)$ and $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ leave commutants of dimensions $14$, $6$ and $2$. The gauge-commuting CPT halvings are $32$ sign patterns times a free pair of lines in the neutral block. Commuting with the total mode number and anomaly freedom cut them to four, differing only in whether the empty or the full five-mode state is the particle half's neutral singlet; the two are exchanged by a swap that commutes with the gauge algebra, so no gauge quantum number decides between them. The grading clause selects the empty state. So the clause is one bit of premise, not derivable from CPT, anomaly freedom and the generation clause (the vacuum-swapped halving satisfies them all); the first line of attack is answered in the negative and the clause stays a premise. Earlier: anomaly freedom with the tower grading as chirality forces odd slot parity and the slot module $(\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2})^{\oplus m}$ (\claimref{synthesis.anomaly-freedom-forces-slot-content}); for two-level slots, slot parity decides (S) (\claimref{synthesis.slot-parity-decides-hypothesis-s}); inside the composite's own five-rung floor two-level slots are odd, and even slots need a spectator generator (\claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}), whence the no-spectator premise (\claimref{standard-model.no-spectator-slots}). The negative clause of \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2) shows any derivation of the lepton must change the state space. A module generated from one vacuum by a doublet of creation operators is a Fock module of the algebra core (\claimref{std-algebra.fock-representation}), and its creation and annihilation operators obey the canonical anticommutation relations (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}). The intermediate gauge algebras are now decided, as a dichotomy: hypercharge grades $\so(10)$ into the number-conserving $\uu(5)$, pair creation and pair annihilation with three disjoint eigenvalue sets, so a gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ either lies in $\uu(5)$, and then the vacuum-swapped halving commutes with it and the bit is free, or contains a pair-creation bilinear and its adjoint, and then that pair with the anomaly-fixed charged chirality forces $\pm(-1)^{N}$, with no use of number conservation. The Pati-Salam, left-right, $\su(4) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \uu(1)$ and flipped $\uu(5)$ stages decide the bit; the Georgi-Glashow $\uu(5)$, and the Standard Model algebra with $B - L$ or the total mode number adjoined, do not (\claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}). On that basis the clause was restated (Leon, 31 October; version 4 of the premise) as "the chirality commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain", equivalent to the grading form for an anomaly-free halving; anomaly freedom is now used to exclude the pair-parity halving $\pm(-1)^{k}$, which also commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra and is anomalous. Since the chain is itself derived under (S), this exchanges the bare choice of the empty state for a requirement on the chain's intermediate stage; it is not a derivation. Other structure is blind to the bit: under the swapped halving the odd-grade Yukawa forms give the neutral singlet no Dirac coupling to the lepton doublet, the Clifford CPT antiunitary treats both halvings alike (same result), and the light-ray array count is sixteen per generation for every CPT halving (\claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}).
(7 November; argued and computed, from a survey of the store.) What \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality} leaves open is the neutral-singlet bit, clause (G) (a unique vacuum, one doublet), clause (f) and the clauses (a) and (b). The neutral-singlet bit is invisible to every structure the swap of the two candidate singlets commutes with: CPT, anomaly freedom, (G), the light-ray count and the Clifford CPT antiunitary all fail to decide it, and no structure in the thermality, entropy, descent or wall subjects breaks the swap, since all of them see only number-conserving or count data. Computed: the gauge algebra with the even pair algebra leaves exactly $\pm(-1)^{N}$ among the anomaly-free CPT halvings and excludes the vacuum-swapped one, and the $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ half of Pati-Salam suffices. Since $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ and the conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ are real forms of one complex algebra (\claimref{standard-model.pair-mixing-not-colour}), the Pati-Salam clause is the conformal invariance of the chirality on the pair factor; what it still needs is the identification of the label copy's parity with the twistor's, which the store's notes call the same missing theorem as (S) and which, with the relative unit sign, would also fix the orientation bit.
attack: Derive the single doublet of slot creation operators ($b = 1$) from the label copy of the pair space that the hierarchy bundle carries.
Derive the joint Clifford system from tower membership of the slot operators, along the no-spectator route.

Derive a gauge stage that leaves $\uu(5)$, the Pati-Salam stage of the chain or another, from the tower without (S); by the dichotomy that would turn the chirality clause into a consequence. The gauge quantum numbers, CPT, anomaly freedom, the generation clause, the light-ray count and the Clifford CPT antiunitary cannot decide the bit.
Resolve the tension that the tower reading at three constituents gives the $32$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(12)$, one generation and its conjugate, not three families.

Clause (G) as a Fock clause: if the slot module is a Fock module of either statistics over its one-slot space, CPT closure forces one doublet and the exterior algebra of it (for two or more doublets the two-slot space carries weak spin one; a symmetric Fock module is infinite-dimensional), so the statistics and the doublet count become outputs (the unique vacuum is part of the Fock clause) and the clause holds automatically if the slot quanta are tower modes (\claimref{synthesis.fock-slot-module-is-cpt-closed-only-over-one-doublet}).

Clause (f) as a Klein convention: the Klein-twisted slot operators obey the same relations as the slot operators, the Pati-Salam generators and the grading are the same operators in both conventions, and the twist is unique up to a central phase, so on the composite's module the joint Clifford system exists canonically (\claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}; \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator} already uses the twist). - >-
  The joint Clifford system from the sign bit: by
  \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}, directions sharing one central sign
  bit, with distinct directions not commuting, generate exactly a Clifford algebra; check whether the clause
  asks for more than that the slot and pair directions are distinct directions sharing one sign bit (the
  adjoint, the signature), and if not, record it as an instance of the foundation postulates.
problem.success: A theorem deriving (S) or its weaker form from stated structure, or one of the five outcomes adopted and recorded in the tier declaration with its consequences carried to T13 and T15.

entities.title: Hypothesis (S): slot statistics, derived from the slot-module hypothesis
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: Under the slot-module hypothesis, the composite's slots are fermionic modes obeying exclusion and forming one Clifford system with its pairs, its state space is the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ with $U(2) \times U(3)$ acting as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$, chirality is the parity of the mode number, and slots of one tower parity whose grading is the chirality are odd.

entities.title: The slot-module hypothesis behind (S)
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: Premise: a composite's state space is a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain once the slots are fermionic (for an anomaly-free halving, equivalently the grading of the joint Clifford system; its content beyond the other clauses and anomaly freedom is the empty-versus-full neutral singlet choice), and slot and pair operators one Clifford system; it yields Hypothesis (S).

entities.title: A gauge algebra decides the neutral-singlet bit exactly when it leaves $\uu(5)$
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ separates $\so(10)$ into $\uu(5)$ and pair creation and annihilation with disjoint eigenvalues, so a gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ either lies in $\uu(5)$, leaving the neutral-singlet bit free, or contains one pair bilinear and its adjoint, which with the anomaly-fixed charged chirality forces $\pm(-1)^{N}$: Pati-Salam, left-right and flipped stages decide the bit, Georgi-Glashow does not; under the swapped choice the singlet has no odd-grade Yukawa pairing in its half, and the Clifford CPT antiunitary is blind to the bit.

entities.title: The Spin(10) clause's content is the choice of neutral singlet
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: On $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ the gauge algebra, $\uu(5)$ and $\so(10)$ have commutants of dimensions $14$, $6$ and $2$; gauge-commuting CPT halvings are $32$ sign patterns times a free pair of neutral lines, $\uu(5)$ (or the total mode number) and anomaly freedom leave four, differing only in whether $\Omega$ or $\Omega^{\top}$ is the particle half's singlet, two choices conjugate under the gauge-commuting swap of the two, and $\Spin(10)$ leaves $\pm(-1)^{N}$, the involutions for which the ten Majoranas are odd: the $\Spin(10)$ clause is that one bit, equivalent to the Clifford grading, and not derivable from the rest.

entities.title: CPT closure forces the slot module; anomaly freedom, the chirality
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: For $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ with $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$, CPT closure holds iff $F = a\Lambda^{0} \oplus b\Lambda^{1} \oplus a\Lambda^{2}$; with one vacuum anomaly-free halvings need $b$ odd, and with $F$ generated from its vacuum CPT closure forces $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ with exclusion and anomaly freedom forces the chirality $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ off the neutral singlets.

entities.title: The automorphisms that preserve the slot/pair split are Pati-Salam
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: Under (S), the automorphisms of the five-mode state space that preserve the slot/pair split form the Pati-Salam group $\mathrm{Spin}(4) \times \mathrm{Spin}(6)$, with $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$ exactly.

entities.title: No spectator generators: a composite's slot operators lie in its own five-rung floor
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: Premise: a composite's slot operators lie in the floor of its own five rungs and borrow no generator from the conformal base $\Cl(2,4)$; for two-level, $U(2)$-covariant slot operators that commute or anticommute with every pair operator, this forces odd slots and (S)'s chirality as the tower grading.

entities.title: Quarks and leptons: the two-level fermion content
entities.subject: standard-model
entities.one_liner: The pair-level cells carry the quark doublet $(2,3)_{1/6}$ unconditionally, and under Hypothesis (S) one slot with the pairs full gives the lepton doublet $(2,1)_{-1/2}$.
